children: China's exports are surging, turbocharged by the artificial-intelligence boom as well as a push by Chinese companies to sell their wares abroad to escape brutal price competition at home. Here are three numbers from newly released August trade data that shed light on a phenomenon that is fueling friction with trading partners over China's growing trade imbalances.
$805 billion: The size of China's total trade surplus for the first eight months of the year, putting it on track to at least match the record $1.2 trillion surplus it recorded in 2025.
130%: The increase in semiconductor exports, by value, in August due to soaring demand for AI. A race to secure the semiconductors needed for new data centers has sharply driven up prices.

34.3%: The increase in exports to the U.S. The rise comes despite an effective tariff rate on Chinese goods that was about 23% in June, according to the Penn Wharton Budget Model-more than triple that of other major trading partners.
